title: Chicken Balti
subtitle: A quick-cooked curry with charred edges and a sharp tomato base
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs in a fast, high-heat sauce of tomatoes, peppers, and whole spices. The balti stays juicy because it spends only minutes in the pan once the sauce is built.
sourceNotes: British-Pakistani balti tradition as developed in Birmingham curry houses from the 1970s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the finished curry for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the sauce and freeze in portions. Add fresh-cooked chicken when reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Add the chicken and finish cooking just before serving.

content.text: A balti is a quick-cooked curry finished in the same pan it is served from. The sauce is sharper and less creamy than a korma or tikka masala, built mainly on tomatoes with whole spices bloomed in oil at the start. Keep the heat high once the chicken goes in so the edges catch slightly rather than stew.
Heat the ghee in the wok over a high heat. Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds to coat the onions.
Add the tinned tomatoes and tomato puree. Cook over a medium heat for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and oil rises to the surface.
Turn the heat back up to high. Add the chicken pieces and stir to coat. Cook for 8 minutes, turning often, until the chicken is cooked through.
Add the peppers and cook for 3 more minutes so they soften slightly but keep some bite.
Stir in the garam masala and salt. Taste and adjust seasoning. Scatter over fresh coriander and serve straight from the wok.

items.cause: The tomatoes were not cooked down enough before the chicken was added.
items.fix: Cook the tomato base until it is thick and oil pools on the surface before adding anything else.

items.symptom: The chicken is dry and tough.
items.cause: It was cooked too long at a low heat and lost its moisture.
items.fix: Keep the heat high and check by cutting a piece after 8 minutes. Remove from heat the moment it is no longer pink.

items.cause: The spices were not cooked in the oil before the tomatoes went in.
items.fix: Add a pinch more garam masala off the heat and a small squeeze of lemon if acidity is lacking.
